sampling_model.design: The identification kernel takes exact population covariances on an arbitrary fixed view graph \(G\). The inherited inference layer may use one sourcewise independent and identically distributed paired sample for each observed edge together with every view-marginal sample.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment variable; the causal target is the finite set of shared-order structural coefficient tuples.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The maintained population has the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view LiMVAM disturbance independence, a shared order, component-aligned cross-view second moments, and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. The generating law need not be Gaussian. Unrestricted LiMVAM laws without component alignment, selection, transport, and arbitrary off-model covariance arrays are excluded.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The new theorem is population-computational. Sampling uncertainty is handled only by the parent covariance-region inversion over empirical edge and marginal covariance blocks; no new rate, limit law, or continuum-region enumerator is claimed.

body.tldr: Many common orders can encode the same coefficient tuple in the restrictive component-aligned LiMVAM class, so traversing every compatible order can be factorial even when the causal output is a singleton. The maintained generating law may be non-Gaussian: it has the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view disturbance independence, together with component-aligned cross-view second moments and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. The population algorithm labels each removed-set transition by the immutable original-label regression row \(\beta(A,r)=\Sigma[r,A]\Sigma[A,A]^{-1}\), prunes dead subset states, interns exact rows, and merges equal live fragments. Arbitrary-view-graph path exactness follows from the generating full covariance; Gaussian coordinate stacks are introduced only to realize an existential compatible completion. The live-fragment congruence and projection charge then enumerate \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) exactly once in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space, with polynomial bit complexity for rational inputs.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier has a \(2^p\)-state compatibility graph but no noncircular way to enumerate distinct numerical tuples without traversing all compatible paths. Published causal enumeration partitions graph classes by graphical effect formulas or lists graph-distinct DAGs, while general quotient enumeration assumes local decomposability not established for covariance-dependent coefficient equality.
project_justification.niche: At a fixed removed set \(A\), every future compatibility test depends only on the Schur residual state, and the row assigned when \(r\) is removed is the immutable original-label regression \(\beta(A,r)\). After source-to-sink pruning, the resulting fragments have nonempty, either identical or disjoint, completion sets.
project_justification.fill: Exact row interning and deterministic integer tries implement the fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. The projection lemma bounds every subset bucket by \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\). On any maintained input, the generating full covariance supplies positive-definite coordinate completions for every candidate order; after the observable path test succeeds, independently assembled Gaussian coordinate stacks realize a compatible completion. This witness construction does not impose Gaussianity on the generating law.

body.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, supplies the shared-order recursive-residual model and orderwise coefficient regressions under ordinary centered finite-second-moment LiMVAM disturbance independence; it does not enumerate the numerical equivalence class left by partial pairing. The present maintained class retains that non-Gaussian input scope while adding the component-aligned cross-view second-moment restriction and strict coordinate covariance positivity. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, Theorems 2--3, motivates quotienting structural representatives by the causal output, but its recursive signatures are graphical total-effect functionals rather than covariance-dependent coefficient rows. WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 1, establishes AMO enumeration; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. Those graph-distinct output counts can remain factorial when many orders share one numerical tuple. WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives the nearest general quotient framework, but its proof relies on local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph; the present right congruence is instead derived from immutable numerical row projections and live-prefix pruning. DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing, demonstrating that projection changes enumeration complexity without treating causal coefficient fibers. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the completion boundary for chordal sparsity patterns; the model-specific theorem here instead uses the generating full covariance as a certificate for an arbitrary view graph on maintained inputs. AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch provides an alternative exact enumeration paradigm but requires a locally searchable parent relation that numerical tuple classes do not supply. Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity supplies the fraction-free minor identity used to prove polynomial certificate height for the rational implementation.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The main total-cost theorem uses an ordered exact-real model and does not imply floating-point stability. A separate theorem proves deterministic output-polynomial bit time and storage for rational maintained-model inputs, including the total emitted encoding length. The result gives a \(2^p\)-state-plus-output bound, not polynomial delay and not a polynomial-in-\(p\) algorithm. The q-only graph construction is certified only for moment collections generated by the maintained non-Gaussian-permitted component-aligned model; an arbitrary off-model nonchordal edge array may pass every local q-test while admitting no positive-semidefinite completion. Exact enumeration over a continuum-valued covariance confidence region is not claimed. The generic write-once dynamic program, row sorting, and integer tries are implementation machinery rather than independent causal contributions.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is confined to exact population enumeration of the coefficient-tuple frontier for the component-aligned shared-order LiMVAM class under an arbitrary fixed pairing graph. Generating disturbances satisfy the ordinary centered finite-second-moment within-view independence condition; cross-view second moments are component aligned and every coordinate disturbance covariance is positive definite. The generating law may be non-Gaussian. Gaussianity is used only to construct one existential full law from the completed coordinate covariance blocks, after path compatibility has been established. The result does not cover unrestricted LiMVAM mechanisms lacking component alignment. The parent covariance-region inversion is reused only as the uncertainty layer after population identification; no new limit law, floating-point guarantee, polynomial-delay result, off-model nonchordal preprocessing guarantee, or finite enumeration of a continuum covariance-region inverse is asserted. The all-zero empty-graph reduction collapses all \(p!\) orders to one tuple, and the rational implementation has polynomial bit complexity in its stated input and output parameters.
